messages:
maya: seeing a sustained throughput drop on prod-dedicated-3 starting ~10:23 UTC. ~40% TPS down and a surge of worker restarts. Putting initial notes here so we don't duplicate — logs attached below.

alex: spotted ~120 restarts in last 45m, most workers hit GPU OOM before clean shutdown. No single model change deployed.

raj: FYI I pulled the runtime profiler — kernels keep switching from attn_vec_fast -> attn_generic in the hot path. Fallbacks correlate with large seq length spikes but also with small-batch traffic that trips a heuristic.

maya: exact log snippet from node gpu-12: 
```
[2026-03-18T10:24:12Z] kernel_select: prefer=attn_vec_fast, fallback=attn_generic, reason=seq_len_mismatch
[2026-03-18T10:24:12Z] allocator: slab_alloc failed size=48MB, arena_free=18MB
[2026-03-18T10:24:12Z] gpu_oom: device=0 pid=32211 signal=OOM
[2026-03-18T10:24:13Z] worker: restart requested (oom), trace=...
```

tina: interesting — profiler shows KV cache eviction rate spiked at the same time (evictions/sec from 12 -> 230). That can fragment the arena and make downstream slab_alloc fail.

sam: I also see batching logs: many small batches (batch_size=1) interleaved with occasional long-seq requests. The batching heuristic is mis-grouping sequences causing kernel to toggle per-batch which prevents kernel-specific memory reuse.

maya: good catch. So likely chain: noisy small-batch traffic -> heuristic forces mixed kernel selection -> attn_generic path allocates larger temporaries -> KV eviction churn fragments arena -> slab_alloc failures -> OOM -> worker restarts -> throughput drop.

raj: quick measurements: during the incident period attn_generic allocations were ~2.3x larger than attn_vec_fast for the same request mix. Also observed CUDA allocator requests pattern: lots of small frees followed by large alloc attempts — classic fragmentation.

perf-bot: perf/telemetry note: 2026-03-18T10:23-10:50: 
- mean p95 latency +120ms 
- TPS -42% 
- worker restarts +118 
- KV eviction rate +18x

oncall-bot: paging oncall rota: @raj assigned as primary for investigation, @tina backup.

alex: immediate mitigations proposed (short-term):
- force kernel pinning for impacted model family to attn_vec_fast (if safe) to avoid per-batch kernel toggles
- raise arena max contiguous free threshold (CUDAMallocArena) to reduce fragmentation pressure
- temporarily increase KV cache capacity for these hosts to reduce eviction churn

maya: agree. I'm +1 on kernel pin to stop oscillation while we do root cause. Any risk of correctness mismatch if we pin? attn_vec_fast handles up to seq_len=2048; fallback was triggered due to our heuristic misclassifying a few requests that had trailing pad tokens. We should add a stricter pre-check not to downgrade.

raj: I'll run a canary patch to pin kernels on two nodes and watch for stability. Also will add histograms for alloc request sizes to find fragmentation hotspots.

sam: medium-term fixes:
- update batching heuristic to prefer homogenous seq-length windows (delay tiny batches <50ms to wait for similar seqs)
- add kernel-selection soft-state so consecutive batches stick to chosen kernel when possible
- KV cache eviction grace window to avoid synchronized eviction storms

tina: last night we landed a change to slab rebalancer (reduced coalescing threshold) that might have increased fragmentation in presence of many small frees. I will revert that change on a subset and compare.

maya: observations from canary (11:05-11:30): pinned nodes show 6% TPS delta vs control but zero OOMs. Control group still seeing sporadic OOMs. Good signal that kernel oscillation is a major amplifier.

raj: action items (short):
- raj: patch to pin kernel selection -> roll canary to 10% (ETA 30m)
- tina: revert last-night slab rebalancer tweak on 4 nodes (ETA 45m)
- alex: bump KV cache capacity on prod-dedicated-3 hosts (ETA 20m)
- sam: draft batching heuristic change and a low-risk rollout path (ETA EOD)
- maya: add alloc-size histograms + KV eviction trace to per-route dashboard (ETA 2h)

maya: I'll keep monitoring. If pin + slab revert gets stable we'll do a broader rollout and then follow up with the batching/kernel logic changes.

tina: noted — I'll log the revert PR and tag this thread.

alex: thanks all. Please post any new logs here.

sam: quick thought — we should add an automated alert when kernel churn > X/min OR KV evictions spike > Y; this would have caught the pattern earlier. Adding to backlog.

maya: agreed. closing interim summary: root cause hypothesis = kernel-selection oscillation combined with KV eviction-driven memory fragmentation causing slab_alloc failures and subsequent OOMs -> worker restarts -> throughput drop. Working fixes: kernel pinning + revert fragmentation regression + KV sizing + batching heuristic improvements.

(ends)
